text: Car ownership rates differ enormously by wealth — the US has about 800 cars per 1,000 people; India has about 30 — a gap that reflects not just wealth but also the quality of public transport infrastructure
The wealthiest 10% of countries account for roughly 70% of all cars on the road — car ownership remains heavily concentrated in North America, Europe, and parts of East Asia
The United States alone has more than 280 million registered passenger cars — roughly one car per adult, and more than any other country by a wide margin
Flying remains one of the most unequally distributed activities on Earth — the majority of flights are taken by a small minority of frequent flyers, mostly in wealthy countries
Most people in low-income countries have never flown — air travel is overwhelmingly the activity of wealthier populations, and the gap between rich and poor countries is enormous
The US alone accounts for roughly a quarter of all commercial passengers globally — more than all of Africa, South America, and the Middle East combined
Electric cars now account for 25% of all new car sales worldwide.
There are more than double the number of EVs in China compared with Europe.
India has approximately 6 million electric vehicles in use as of 2026.
